patch.value: Release ratchet verdicts are a property of the working copy, not the commit: gitignored installs and clone-local git config decide three populations, so an identical commit passes locally and fails in CI

The gate materializes a commit view containing exactly the files the next commit would carry (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard) and measures there; a --working-copy escape hatch and an explicit --pm-path both bypass it; A fresh clone of the same commit and a maintainer working copy produce byte-identical observed populations for every declared selector; The receipt names the measurement scope so a reader can tell which tree produced the verdict; Unit coverage exercises commit-view materialization, the hardlink-to-copy fallback, the pending-deletion path, and the working-copy bypass
The tracker measurement ratchet returns the same verdict for a given commit on every machine, so a maintainer can reproduce and pre-empt the hosted result before pushing.

On 2026-08-05 the gate exited 0 on a maintainer checkout and exited 1 on the identical commit in the v2026.8.5 tag-push release run, blocking the release pipeline. Three populations diverged: validate_files_missing_linked_paths 195 local vs 204 hosted, health_check:integrity ok local vs warn hosted, and validate_merge_driver_configuration absent local vs 5 hosted (an undeclared population, which fails closed).

message: Filed from a reproduced CI/local divergence on the v2026.8.5 release run; duplicate check: pm-ips23h (closed, built the ratchet), pm-kpftft (closed, built the tracker data-quality CI gate), pm-ei6x66 (open, general local/hosted gate parity) — none covers environment-conditioned observation.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Reproduction (2026-08-05, HEAD 8845ec884): cloned this checkout with 'git clone --depth 1 file://<repo>' and ran the same three measurement commands against both trees. Working copy: validate_files_missing_linked_paths=195, no validate_merge_driver_configuration warning, health integrity=ok. Fresh clone of the identical commit: 204, validate_merge_driver_configuration=5, health integrity=warn. Byte-for-byte the same commit, opposite verdicts.

Causes, both proven:
1. The 9-path delta is exactly .agents/pm/extensions/pm-changelog and 8 files beneath it. .gitignore line 27 ignores .agents/pm/extensions/*, so an installed package resolves only for the maintainer who ran pm install. A full untruncated diff (validate --check-files --verbose-file-lists) showed the working-copy set is a strict subset of the clone set with no path in the other direction.
2. The merge driver lives in clone-local git config written by 'pm merge install' and carried by no commit. pm health folds that audit into its integrity status, so one uninstallable git-config fact drove two of the three divergences.

Fix: the gate now measures a commit view built from 'git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard', which is exactly what the next commit would carry, derived from committed ignore rules, and has no .git so every clone-local audit is skipped rather than answered per machine. Uncommitted work stays visible so --update and pre-push checks still measure what the author is about to publish.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Verification: the gate now fails locally with the exact CI message (validate-files-missing-linked-paths declared 195, observed 204), which is the first time the hosted verdict was reproducible on a maintainer machine. After re-baselining that one declaration to the environment-invariant 204 the gate exits 0 in both modes: 'passed (19 enforced, 0 retired, 2320 items, commit view of 5905 committable files)' and 'passed (... working copy)'. Materialization costs ~4s for 5905 files via hardlinks.

The 195 baseline was not a regression that got absorbed: it was measured through a working copy that hid 9 members, so the true population was always 204. Shrinking it below 195 means removing dangling links from ten legacy closed items whose closed_at is null, which reorders the changelog until pm-wrbe lands; pm-j8z6 owns that burn-down and the ratchet holds the line at 204 meanwhile.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Typed edges: implements the GA stability milestone, discovered from the chronically failing scheduled release, verifies the local/hosted parity contract

patch.value: It now does: the gate first reproduced the hosted failure locally for the first time, then passed identically in commit-view and working-copy modes.
The same commit yields the same ratchet verdict on every machine.

Added materializeCommitView and contextForCommitView to the gate, routed the default measurement pass through the view, kept --working-copy and an explicit --pm-path as bypasses, and re-baselined the one honestly mis-measured declaration from 195 to 204 with the reason recorded in the declaration note.

The tracker measurement ratchet now measures a commit view — the exact file set the next commit would carry, built from git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, with no .git — so its verdict is a property of the commit rather than of whoever's machine ran it. The two environment facts that split the verdict are neutralized at the source: gitignored installed packages under .agents/pm/extensions are absent from the view in every environment, and clone-local merge-driver git config is unreadable there, so pm health integrity stops flipping on it. A maintainer checkout and a fresh clone of the same commit now report identical populations for all 19 declared selectors.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Closed-loop verification: CI run 31036617924 on main is green end to end, including the Gates (static) job whose tracker-measurement step was the release blocker. The same job failed on the two commits before it for two further reasons this fix surfaced rather than caused — an eslint rule the local static gate never runs, and a coverage threshold the local coverage command prints but does not enforce (now filed as pm-2qqcgl). Both are recorded on pm-ei6x66 as the other direction of the same parity gap.
